flashcards.q: Why does a prompt diff carry zero behavioral information?
flashcards.a: A code diff tells you what the program will do differently; a prompt diff tells you what the string says differently. The mapping from wording to behavior is a black box measurable only through evals. So the eval gate, not the diff review, is the safety net.

flashcards.q: The staged rollout ramp and its guardrail metrics.
flashcards.a: 1% for >=1h, 10% for 24-48h, then 100%. Guardrails: task completion (primary), schema-validity <99% -> instant revert, cost/step >1.15x baseline (excluding post-flip cache warm-up), p95 latency >1.25x baseline. Auto-revert = repoint the production label, <1 min, no deploy.

id, version, template (typed variables), model (pinned, never 'latest'), params (temp/top_p/max_tokens), schema_out, few_shots (versioned WITH template), eval_scores (with golden-set id), status (draft/staged/live/rolled_back), labels (production/staging/draft), author + why-note.

flashcards.q: Why must traffic split be a sticky hash, never per-request random?
flashcards.a: 1) Users feel mid-conversation personality flips. 2) Per-request randomization thrashes the prompt cache (conversation bounces between two prefixes, neither stays warm). 3) Per-request assignment makes per-user metrics non-independent, invalidating the statistics. Split = sha256(prompt_id + user_id) mod 100.

flashcards.q: Why is model config part of the versioned artifact?
flashcards.a: Behavior = template + model + sampling params + example order. Temperature 0.0 -> 0.7 is a bigger behavioral change than most wording edits. Versioning the string while hot-editing config leaves the registry lying about what produced last week's traces.

flashcards.q: Semver for prompts: what is MAJOR vs MINOR vs PATCH?
flashcards.a: MAJOR = contract change (output schema, tool vocabulary, refusal policy, task definition). MINOR = wording, few-shot order, added example. PATCH = typo. Eval gate applies to ALL three, because intent is not a guarantee — PATCH changes have regressed double digits.

flashcards.q: Prompt caching: why does editing the system prompt invalidate the cache, and what are the 2026 price multipliers?
flashcards.a: Prefix cache = exact match; hierarchy tools -> system -> messages, a change at any level kills that level and everything after. Reads 0.1x base input (~90% discount), writes 1.25x (5m TTL) or 2x (1h); OpenAI GPT-5.6-gen defaults to 30m TTL, 1,024-token minimum. A stable change is cheap: one 1.25x write, break-even ~1.4 reuses.

flashcards.q: What is the chronic cache killer (not versioning), and its observable symptom?
flashcards.a: Interpolated values (timestamp, user name) inside the cached system prefix -> prefix is unique per request -> never caches -> ~10x input cost on that segment forever. Symptom: cache hit rate falls 90% -> ~0 with no deploy, no model change, no code diff.

flashcards.q: Canary at n=400 shows 81% vs control 84% (n=3600). Revert?
flashcards.a: SE_diff = sqrt(0.81*0.19/400 + 0.84*0.16/3600) ~= 2.1%, so 3 points is ~1.4 sigma = noise. Don't confirm regression. Two-tier policy: absolute floor (any arm < 0.70 completion reverts at ANY n) + statistical rule (2 sigma, n >= 100/arm). Small canaries only catch BIG regressions; a confirmed 3-pt drop needs ~2,500/arm.

flashcards.q: Auto-revert policy: the two tiers plus hysteresis.
flashcards.a: Tier 1 immediate, non-statistical: schema-validity <99%, guardrail hits >2x baseline, completion <0.70 floor. Tier 2 statistical (n >= 100/arm): completion < baseline - 2*SE, cost/step >1.15x, p95 >1.25x. Hysteresis: same version auto-reverts twice -> quarantine (rolled_back, human must clear it) or the system flaps at 2am.

flashcards.q: The eval gate formula, and how epsilon is set.
flashcards.a: new_score >= old_score - epsilon, computed not felt. epsilon = the eval's own jitter: run the same version twice on the golden set and record the spread (typically 1-3 points on a 50-100 item set). The golden set needs 50-100+ real items with verifiers, adversarial cases, and a held-out slice — 12 items is gate theater.

flashcards.q: When is prompt versioning the wrong investment?
flashcards.a: Solo tool/prototype with one author (git + tags IS the registry; a service is ops burden). Genuinely frozen low-stakes prompts. Orgs where changes are really model-config changes (version the config, same machinery). Test: if this prompt regresses silently tomorrow, who notices and how fast? Users-in-days -> full pipeline; engineer-immediately -> versioning only; nobody -> don't build it.
